Army Black Knights.status: Returning starter — split time to a degree with Dewayne Coleman in 2025.
Army Black Knights.career_experience: Established starter in Army's option offense.
Army Black Knights.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Army Black Knights.passing: 694 passing yards with four passing touchdowns.
Army Black Knights.rushing: 304 carries for 1,223 yards and 18 touchdowns — nearly 41% of Army's carries.
Army Black Knights.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a completion rate. Team-level: Army fell from 5.7 yards per carry in 2024 conference games to 4.38 in 2025.
Army Black Knights.turnovers: Not addressed in guide individually; the guide notes Army is +12 in turnover margin across two years of conference play while granting its style limits turnover volume.
Army Black Knights.competition: None described — Hellums is the settled starter.
Army Black Knights.backup: No game experience behind him, which the guide names as a specific risk. It allows Monken and coordinator Cody Worley may have found something in converted quarterback Godspower Nwawuihe, who ran for 171 yards in the Fenway Bowl.
Army Black Knights.author_confidence: Concerned about durability rather than ability. The guide's stated worry is workload — a brutal load for a 5-foot-10 player that must be factored into any long-term position on Army.
Army Black Knights.positive_case: 1,223 rushing yards and 18 touchdowns plus four passing scores, in a scheme he runs as the established starter.
Army Black Knights.concerns: Workload and durability, and the absence of game experience behind him: the guide says a Hellums injury would be brutal.
Army Black Knights.scheme_fit: Established — he is the incumbent in Army's option system under coordinator Cody Worley.
Army Black Knights.supporting_cast: Thinned. With Noah Short, Hayden Reed, Dewayne Coleman and Briggs Bartosh all gone, the guide stresses somebody must take carries off Hellums.
Army Black Knights.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 7.5 wins. The guide names a Hellums injury as a specific risk given no experience behind him, and its core statistical argument is a reversal: Army was outgained by nearly a full yard per play in conference play, against outgaining conference foes by nearly 1.2 yards per play in 2024. Situationally, Army plays at a rest disadvantage in each of its first three October games. Projection is 6.92 wins.
Army Black Knights.outlook_dependency: Very high, and specifically on availability. The guide states a Hellums injury would be brutal because nothing is behind him.

Charlotte 49ers.status: Transfer — from Western Carolina; described as a stopgap, with the job possibly falling to him only until Conner Harrell returns.
Charlotte 49ers.passing: Not addressed in guide for Gonzales. For the alternatives: Conner Harrell posted 66.7% completions and a 4-to-2 ratio before a season-ending injury; Grayson Loftis an 8-to-8 ratio on 55% completions.
Charlotte 49ers.efficiency: Not addressed in guide for Gonzales.
Charlotte 49ers.turnovers: Not addressed in guide for Gonzales.
Charlotte 49ers.competition: Unsettled and injury-driven. The guide says the job may fall to Gonzales until Harrell returns, and that Harrell — probably the best quarterback on the roster — will be out until around mid-October.
Charlotte 49ers.backup: Conner Harrell (North Carolina), out until around mid-October, and Grayson Loftis (Duke). Zach Wilcke took reps last season and has moved on.
Charlotte 49ers.author_confidence: Very low, and stated bluntly: none of the options are particularly good.
Charlotte 49ers.positive_case: The guide offers none at quarterback. Its consolation is elsewhere — almost all the backs and receivers are new, which it says can only help after 4.6 yards per play.
Charlotte 49ers.concerns: The best option is unavailable until around mid-October, and the guide rates none of the available options particularly good.
Charlotte 49ers.supporting_cast: Almost entirely new at the skill positions, and structurally weak up front. The guide identifies a multi-year problem: Charlotte is not big or strong enough in the trenches, at -2.3 in yards-per-carry differential last year and -1.6 the year before, and has not exceeded 20 sacks since 2019.
Charlotte 49ers.portal_context: Gonzales from Western Carolina joins Harrell and Loftis, both added last season when boosters funded a real attempt. Neither the incoming class nor the portal class graded highly for 247Sports relative to the conference, but the guide notes there are many more bodies.
Charlotte 49ers.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 2.5 wins. The guide expects the on-field product to improve while judging two additional wins a chore, and names Harrell's absence until mid-October as a specific reason. Projection is 1.81 wins.
Charlotte 49ers.outlook_dependency: Very high. Quarterback availability is one of the two stated reasons for the Under alongside depth.
Charlotte 49ers.conflicts: The team appears in two projected standings tables in the guide's conference previews, a source error recorded in the Conference Database. It does not bear on the quarterback record.

Connecticut Huskies.status: New starter, identity undetermined — the guide states there is no clear starting quarterback and many position battles.
Connecticut Huskies.previous_school: Kalieb Osborne comes from Toledo; Jake Merklinger from Tennessee.
Connecticut Huskies.competition: Open and explicitly unresolved. Kalieb Osborne, a Toledo player who followed Jason Candle, will compete with Tennessee's Jake Merklinger and in-house options.
Connecticut Huskies.backup: The named candidates are Kalieb Osborne and Jake Merklinger, plus unspecified in-house options.
Connecticut Huskies.author_confidence: Low. The guide states there is no clear starting quarterback and says the offense has major question marks.
Connecticut Huskies.positive_case: Not addressed in guide at quarterback; the guide's positive case is the defense, since coordinator Ryan Manalac is a Pat Narduzzi disciple and Toledo ranked second nationally in yards allowed per game.
Connecticut Huskies.concerns: No clear starter, and UConn ranks 138th in Phil Steele's Experience chart — which the guide notes is officially dead last now that North Dakota State and Sacramento State are in FBS.
Connecticut Huskies.scheme_fit: Coordinator Nunzio Campanile was at Syracuse from 2023-25 and Rutgers before; the guide finds it surprising that a decade-long Toledo head coach has so many new colleagues.
Connecticut Huskies.supporting_cast: Thin and unfamiliar. The guide notes even the transfers are largely not recognizable names, the exception being K'Von Sherman with 93 tackles at Toledo. Running back Kenji Christian is at his fourth school, most recently Toledo, and three potential offensive line starters were together at Toledo without playing much.
Connecticut Huskies.portal_context: Candle brought some Toledo players so he is not starting with zero familiar faces, but the guide identifies the specific shortfall: none of his extremely productive offensive players followed, and only a couple on defense.
Connecticut Huskies.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins, and the guide is explicit that the coaching transition is not its whole reason. Despite only five road games it expects UConn to fall short of bowl eligibility. It closes with the bar UConn is falling from — 31.9 and 35.3 points per game the last two seasons and 6.7 yards per play last year — and says the fan base probably will not see those numbers. Projection is 5.39 wins.
Connecticut Huskies.outlook_dependency: High. The guide separates the sides explicitly: the offense has major question marks while the defense has a good chance of being solid.
Connecticut Huskies.conflicts: The guide declines to name a starter, so this record carries no VSiN preseason expectation for the position.

East Carolina Pirates.status: New starter, identity undetermined — the guide calls this the biggest personnel question and names two options without choosing.
East Carolina Pirates.previous_school: Emory Williams comes from Miami; Mitch Griffis from Texas Tech, his fourth school.
East Carolina Pirates.career_experience: Mitch Griffis is a four-time transfer, at Texas Tech last season. Emory Williams' experience is not addressed.
East Carolina Pirates.competition: Open. The guide names Miami transfer Emory Williams and four-time transfer Mitch Griffis as the main options — Williams bigger and more athletic, Griffis closer to Drew Mestemaker's skill set though lacking his size — and flags that a possibly shaky offensive line early may favour Williams.
East Carolina Pirates.backup: The two named candidates are Emory Williams and Mitch Griffis; the guide does not rank them.
East Carolina Pirates.author_confidence: Positive about the outcome without picking a player. The guide expects good numbers either way, noting Katin Houser, another Harrell portal find, was very solid last season, and credits Harrell with a finger on the pulse of free agency.
East Carolina Pirates.positive_case: Blake Harrell's track record with portal quarterbacks, plus a scheme change to a system that led the nation in scoring at over 45 points and in yards at just over 512 per game.
East Carolina Pirates.concerns: Neither option is established, and a possibly shaky offensive line early could constrain whoever starts.
East Carolina Pirates.scheme_fit: New coordinator Jordan Davis brings a scheme change, having worked under Eric Morris at North Texas. The guide corrects a likely assumption with data: a Morris offense is not merely a chuck-it attack, since Mestemaker threw 463 times for nearly 4,400 yards while Caleb Hawkins carried 231 times for 1,434 yards on 517 team rushing attempts. Griffis is described as closer to Mestemaker's skill set.
East Carolina Pirates.supporting_cast: Almost entirely new — virtually none of last season's major contributors return. Davis brought backup back Ashton Gray and receiver Landon Sides, so some players know the scheme, and with the run game having fallen from 4.8 to 4.1 yards per carry the guide sees a good chance of recovery.
East Carolina Pirates.portal_context: Williams from Miami, Griffis from Texas Tech, Gray and Sides following coordinator Jordan Davis. Harrell also works with two new coordinators after his previous ones left for Ole Miss and South Florida.
East Carolina Pirates.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins, with the guide stressing East Carolina will have to earn 8-4 or better. The offsetting factor is that East Carolina avoids UTSA and Tulane, two of the four teams that beat it last season. Projection is 7.72 wins.
East Carolina Pirates.outlook_dependency: High as a question, moderate as a risk. The guide calls quarterback the biggest personnel question while expecting good numbers either way.
East Carolina Pirates.conflicts: The guide names two candidates and declines to state an expected starter, so this record carries no VSiN preseason expectation for the position.

Florida Atlantic Owls.status: Returning starter — the guide calls him effectively the only starting option.
Florida Atlantic Owls.previous_school: Western Kentucky — the guide compares his three seasons there with his Florida Atlantic season.
Florida Atlantic Owls.career_experience: Three seasons at Western Kentucky before Florida Atlantic.
Florida Atlantic Owls.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Florida Atlantic Owls.passing: Not addressed in guide as a yardage line; the guide records 17 interceptions in 2025 against only 11 in three seasons at Western Kentucky.
Florida Atlantic Owls.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a rate.
Florida Atlantic Owls.turnovers: 17 interceptions — the single figure the guide builds the team's case around, since Florida Atlantic was -21 in turnover margin. It defends him partially: he was asked to throw a lot and Florida Atlantic trailed often, and he had only 11 interceptions in three seasons at Western Kentucky. It ends on a genuine silver lining — seven interceptions came in the first three games and six in the last three, so he protected the ball through the middle of the season.
Florida Atlantic Owls.competition: Effectively none — the guide says he is effectively the only starting option.
Florida Atlantic Owls.backup: Rice transfer Drew Devillier and redshirt freshman Jordan Magwood, who threw nine passes.
Florida Atlantic Owls.author_confidence: Sympathetic and qualified. The guide divides responsibility rather than blaming one player, noting coordinator Brett Dewhurst's defense forced only eight turnovers.
Florida Atlantic Owls.positive_case: A much lower interception rate across three Western Kentucky seasons, a mid-season stretch in which he protected the ball, and year two in the system with more talent around him.
Florida Atlantic Owls.concerns: 17 interceptions, and a structural problem the guide identifies precisely: Easton Messer, who caught 104 balls for 1,052 yards, is still the only true go-to target, which could keep holding Veltkamp and the team back.
Florida Atlantic Owls.scheme_fit: Year two under Zach Kittley, the youngest head coach in FBS and a big Air Raid proponent, who also did double duty as coordinator in his first head-coaching year and has had far more time to evaluate fits.
Florida Atlantic Owls.supporting_cast: Thin at the top and weak on the ground. The guide calls the rushing numbers laughable — 105 yards per game at 3.5 per carry, falling to 82 yards and 2.9 in American play — and offers a possible explanation in the line shifting to a very pass-heavy blocking scheme. It finds the running back room more intriguing: Kaden Shields-Dutton averaged 5.5 yards per carry and Kittley went the junior college route for Leonard Farrow, who averaged over seven at Fairmont State.
Florida Atlantic Owls.portal_context: 30 portal additions including defenders capable of creating negative plays; Drew Devillier arrives from Rice and Leonard Farrow from Fairmont State.
Florida Atlantic Owls.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 5.5 wins. The guide is unusually explicit about conviction, calling this not a strong opinion but a lean: a 4-8 team with a -21 turnover margin now has more talent in year two of the system. It expects another high-variance team given heavy pass volume, and argues cleaning up the turnover margin could change everything. Projection is 5.64 wins.
Florida Atlantic Owls.outlook_dependency: Very high. The guide's whole case turns on the turnover margin, and 17 of the giveaways were the quarterback's interceptions.

Memphis Tigers.status: New starter, identity undetermined — the guide names three candidates for an essentially brand-new roster.
Memphis Tigers.previous_school: Marcus Stokes comes from West Florida; Air Noland from South Carolina, having previously been at Ohio State; Denzel Gardner is a Huff recruit.
Memphis Tigers.career_experience: Marcus Stokes was a multi-year West Florida starter; Air Noland was a highly touted recruit who never played at Ohio State before transferring to South Carolina.
Memphis Tigers.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as counts.
Memphis Tigers.competition: Open among three named candidates — Stokes, Noland or Huff recruit Denzel Gardner — with the guide declining to pick.
Memphis Tigers.backup: The three named candidates are Marcus Stokes, Air Noland and Denzel Gardner.
Memphis Tigers.author_confidence: Interested rather than confident. The guide calls the fit of all the transfer pieces fascinating to watch and frames its Over as a bet on the coach.
Memphis Tigers.positive_case: Coordinator Kevin Decker's record — an Old Dominion offense ranked top-20 in yards per play at 32 points per game, and a 2021 Fordham offense averaging over 600 yards per game.
Memphis Tigers.concerns: No established starter and, as the guide puts it, no truly established skill players whoever wins the job.
Memphis Tigers.scheme_fit: Described precisely: Decker's philosophy is high-octane and explosive, but starts with the ground game with the pass coming off it — Old Dominion averaged 5.6 yards per carry and nearly 240 rushing yards.
Memphis Tigers.supporting_cast: Unproven by design. Dallan Hayden averaged over five yards per carry at Ohio State but was ineffective at Colorado; Jaylin Carter had 166 yards at Southern Miss; Manny Covey had under 300 yards in three seasons at Cincinnati. Receivers are similar, with some impressive yards-per-reception figures but few catches. The guide reframes this as a coherent roster philosophy rather than a random collection: noteworthy recruits who could not crack lineups elsewhere, all carrying chips on their shoulders.
Memphis Tigers.portal_context: Essentially a brand-new roster for Charles Huff, built around players discarded or cast off elsewhere, with several Southern Miss players following him on defense.
Memphis Tigers.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins, stated as a bet on the coach — two good coordinator hires, and a sense Huff has motivated players discarded elsewhere. The non-conference schedule is tough with UNLV and Boise State, but the conference slate is not bad, and the guide notes Huff has six games before the New Orleans trip to get the team in shape. Projection is 7.38 wins.
Memphis Tigers.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The guide's Over is explicitly a bet on the coach and the coordinators rather than on any named quarterback.
Memphis Tigers.conflicts: The guide names three candidates and declines to state an expected starter, so this record carries no VSiN preseason expectation for the position.

Navy Midshipmen.status: New starter — promoted from within after Blake Horvath exhausted eligibility.
Navy Midshipmen.career_experience: Started games in each of the last two seasons when Horvath was banged up, and knows the scheme.
Navy Midshipmen.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a count; the guide records starts in each of the last two seasons.
Navy Midshipmen.passing: A 46.3% career completion rate — set directly against Horvath's 58.8%, which trailed only Roger Staubach among Navy passers with at least 120 attempts.
Navy Midshipmen.competition: None described — Woodson is presented as the successor.
Navy Midshipmen.author_confidence: Guarded, with the gap quantified. The guide says he has enormous shoes to fill and identifies the specific shortfall as accuracy.
Navy Midshipmen.positive_case: He knows the scheme, has started games in each of the last two seasons, and averaged 9.4 yards per carry on 44 attempts.
Navy Midshipmen.concerns: Accuracy — 46.3% against Horvath's 58.8% — and the scale of what has left around him.
Navy Midshipmen.scheme_fit: Established. Coordinator Drew Cronic's Wing-T modified triple option gives opponents much to prepare for, and Woodson knows it.
Navy Midshipmen.supporting_cast: Devastated. Alex Tecza ran for 902 yards at 5.7 per carry with 10 touchdowns and finished 12th in Navy rushing yards at 2,236; all-time leading receiver Eli Heidenreich, a seventh-round Steelers pick, had over 500 rushing yards and 941 receiving yards on 51 catches; fourth-leading rusher and second-leading receiver Brandon Chatman also exhausted eligibility. The guide quantifies the hole: Navy is missing 93.5% of its passing yards, over 83% of its rushing yards and over 84% of its receiving yards.
Navy Midshipmen.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 7.5 wins. The conference schedule is not too demanding and Navy should again be better than both service academies, but the guide concludes that with two years of film on the Cronic offense and massive personnel losses, heavy regression is possible — while candidly noting its own projection is 7.56 wins.
Navy Midshipmen.outlook_dependency: Very high. The guide poses the central question as whether Navy's production came from Cronic's scheme or from a generational run of offensive leaders, with Horvath first among them.
Navy Midshipmen.conflicts: The guide gives Brian Newberry's tenure differently in two places, described in the Team Database from pp. 49 and 60. It does not bear on the quarterback record.

North Texas Eagles.status: Transfer — the guide calls him the clubhouse leader rather than a confirmed starter.
North Texas Eagles.previous_school: UCF; previously Indiana and originally Tennessee.
North Texas Eagles.career_experience: Originally went to Tennessee and started games for Indiana and UCF; this is his first non-Power Four team.
North Texas Eagles.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a count; the guide records starts at Indiana and UCF.
North Texas Eagles.turnovers: Characterized rather than counted: the guide says he has not taken great care of the football.
North Texas Eagles.competition: The guide calls him the clubhouse leader at quarterback without naming rivals.
North Texas Eagles.author_confidence: Low. The guide notes he steps down in class with his first non-Power Four team but has not taken great care of the football.
North Texas Eagles.positive_case: Genuine Power Four starting experience at Indiana and UCF, on a roster where the guide says most players simply did not latch on at their previous schools.
North Texas Eagles.concerns: Ball security, and a supporting cast the guide describes as possibly the most stripped-down programme it has seen.
North Texas Eagles.scheme_fit: Uncertain. Neal Brown will call his own plays, which the guide says may work well or not at all, qualifying his record: Troy did not play with much tempo or light up scoreboards, though it scored 30-plus in each of his last three seasons, and West Virginia averaged 30-plus in only two of six.
North Texas Eagles.supporting_cast: Almost nothing returns. The top returning rusher had 95 yards on 21 carries, the top pass catcher seven grabs for 80 yards, the top tackler 32 stops and 1.5 sacks, the top defensive back four pass breakups — and even the kicker and punter are gone. Jahiem White averaged 6.5 yards per carry at West Virginia and rejoins Brown.
North Texas Eagles.portal_context: The roster is described as players who barely featured plus transfers from every corner of the country; Jackson, White and Aaron Alexander (91 tackles at Arkansas State) are the named exceptions.
North Texas Eagles.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins. The schedule opens at Indiana, then hosts UNLV before a trip to Texas State, with further road games at Navy, UTSA and Tulane. Its structural read is that the home games are all attainable but North Texas might lose every road game, leaving no margin for error at home. Projection is 5.81 wins, and it states plainly that it still likes the Under.
North Texas Eagles.outlook_dependency: High. The guide names the quarterback's ball security among its reasons for the Under despite a projection above the number.
